segments: ...of the Island (Jazirat Ibn Umar), when they learned that the thread of the life of Mongke Timur had already been cut,
seized Safi Qarqubi and his son and his servant,
and stripped them naked and paraded them through the markets of the Island,
and put them to an evil death.
Abaqa, king of kings, set out from Baghdad,
and came to the city of Hamadan.
And on Easter Sunday of that same year 1593 [of the Greeks = 1282 AD],
he went to the church in it,
and rejoiced on the feast with the Christians.
And on Monday, a certain Persian nobleman,
whose name was Bihnam,
made a banquet for him in his house.
And on the night preceding Tuesday he became agitated,
and kept seeing apparitions in the air.
And in the morning hours of Wednesday of White Week (Easter Week),
the first of Nisan,
and the twentieth of the eleventh month of the Ishmaelites (Dhu al-Qada),
he departed from this world.
And in that same Nisan, on the twenty-sixth of it, on a Sunday,
the sixteenth of Muharram,
his brother Mongke Timur also departed from this life in the territory of the Island.
For after Abaqa's decease, the nobles had sent an envoy to him, saying to him:
"There is no order for you to go to Syria,"
without letting him know about the decease of his brother.
And so both of these brothers, kings of the world, passed away,
without either of them perceiving the death of his brother.
And after a few days,
about six thousand horsemen came from Syria,
and crossed the Euphrates,
and went as far as Jazirat Qardu.
And Mumin, the governor of the city, went out and encountered them,
and was defeated and captured;
and, being bound, was taken away to Egypt.
And panic fell upon the territory of Nineveh,
and all the inhabitants of the country fled to the monastery of Mar Mattai.
And they were in great distress,
and a plague fell among them,
and about thirty souls of the monks died.
At this time a certain Persian secretary,
whose name was Majd al-Mulk,
accused Ala al-Din, the Sahib Diwan of Baghdad,
and showed that he had embezzled a great amount from the revenues of the public treasury.
And Ala al-Din was arrested,
and was stripped of everything that he possessed,
so that even his young sons were sold to merchants.
And while he was in this distress,
Abaqa died,
and Ahmad was made king,
and he killed Majd al-Mulk,
the secretary who had denounced Ala.
